To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
workplace ostracization leads to lower person organization fit, which in turn leads to lower organizational citizenship behavior and higher deviant behavior.

workplace ostracized employees who perceive a fit with their organizations will be more likely to engage in organizational citizenship behavior and less likely to engage in deviant behavior than those employees who are not perceived to be a fit with the organization.

person organization fit mediates the relationships between workplace and both organizational citizenship behaviors and deviant behaviors, while perceived organizational supports moderates the relationship between person organization fit, organizational citizenship behavior and person organization fit, deviant behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how workplace ostracism is associated with person organization fit and behavioral outcomes.
the role of person organization in workplace ostracism.
the mediating and moderating effects of workplace environment on the relationship between workplace environment and organizational behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of this study support the mediating role of person organization in the relationship between ostracism and organizational citizenship behavior and the mediating role between person organization fit in the relationship between person organization fit, workplace ostracism on deviant behavior, and the moderating role of perceived organizational support in person organization fit on both organizational citizenship behavior, deviant behavior, respectively.

the results of this study support the mediating role of person organization in the relationship between perceived ostracism and organizational behavior and the moderating role of perceived organizational support in this relationship.
the more a person perceives workplace ostracism from the organization, the more the person perceives a poor fit with the organization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
workplace ostracization is an antecedent to both organizational citizenship behavior as well as deviant behavior.
person organization fit and organizational support play a critical role in understanding the relationship between workplace environment and employee behavior.
person organization fit and its interaction with perceived organizational support can explain the behavioral consequences of workplace ostracism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the negative effects of workplace ostracism on employees' organizational citizenship behavior and their deviant behavior can be reduced when person organization fit is strong.

workplace ostracization can lead to deviant behaviors, but the extent of the impact is contingent upon the person-organization fit of the individual and the perceived organizational support of the organization.
person organization fit and organizational citizenship behavior are important for organizational effectiveness, and perceived organizational support can help employees cope with workplace ostracism.
